entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

<result>## 1. Location

`consolidateDuplicateBonusProducts` is at **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/bonus-product/cart.js:564`** (path as you gave it — correct).

The actual merge is **not** in that function. It delegates to a private helper, `aggregateBonusProductQuantities`, at **`cart.js:78`**. That is where all the field handling lives.

## 2. What it merges, and on what key

`cart.js:573-586`:

```js
    productItems.forEach((item) => {
        if (item.bonusProductLineItem) {
            bonusProducts.push(item)
        } else {
            regularProducts.push(item)
        }
    })

    // Consolidate duplicate bonus products by productId
    const consolidatedBonusProducts = aggregateBonusProductQuantities(bonusProducts)

    // Combine regular products with consolidated bonus products
    // Keep regular products first, then bonus products
    return [...regularProducts, ...consolidatedBonusProducts]
```

- Only items with truthy `item.bonusProductLineItem` are candidates. Regular lines pass through byte-identical and are **reordered to the front**.
- Merge key is **`productId` alone**. Not `bonusDiscountLineItemId`, not `shipmentId`, not price, not `itemId`.

## 3. Exactly which numeric fields are summed / recomputed / carried over

The whole merge, `cart.js:78-98`:

```js
const aggregateBonusProductQuantities = (bonusItems) => {
    const productQuantityMap = new Map()

    bonusItems.forEach((item) => {
        const existingQuantity = productQuantityMap.get(item.productId) || 0
        productQuantityMap.set(item.productId, existingQuantity + (item.quantity || 0))
    })

    const result = []
    productQuantityMap.forEach((quantity, productId) => {
        const sampleItem = bonusItems.find((item) => item.productId === productId)
        if (sampleItem) {
            result.push({
                ...sampleItem,
                quantity: quantity
            })
        }
    })

    return result
}
```

`sampleItem` is `bonusItems.find(...)` — the **first** bonus line with that `productId`. The merged object is that first line spread wholesale, with exactly one key overwritten.

| Field | Treatment |
|---|---|
| `quantity` | **Summed** (`cart.js:83`), `\|\| 0` guard for missing |
| `price` | **Carried over unchanged from the first line.** Not summed, not recomputed |
| `basePrice` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `priceAfterItemDiscount` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `priceAfterOrderDiscount` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `pricePerUnit` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `adjustedTax` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `tax` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `taxBasis` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |

Nothing is summed except `quantity`. Nothing is recomputed. There is no field-specific logic at all — the spread is blind, so any field you name that isn't `quantity` is first-line-wins.

## 4. Is the merged `price` coherent with the merged `quantity`?

**No.** `quantity` becomes `Σ qᵢ` while `price` stays `line₀.price` (which, per the house convention below, is line₀'s *line total*, i.e. `unit × q₀`). So on a merged item:

```
price / quantity  ==  (unit × q₀) / Σqᵢ     ≠  unit
```

Two bonus lines of qty 1 at unit 100 merge to `{quantity: 2, price: 100}` → `price/quantity = 50`. Under-reports by a factor of N for N equal-quantity lines.

**Severity caveat worth knowing before you act on this:** the canonical SFCC bonus line shape is all-zeros on money. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/mocks/mock-data.js:5739-5757` — `adjustedTax: 0, basePrice: 0, price: 0, priceAfterItemDiscount: 0, priceAfterOrderDiscount: 0, tax: 0, taxBasis: 0`, and **`pricePerUnit` is absent entirely**. For a 100%-off bonus, `0 / anything === 0`, so the incoherence is latent. It becomes a real wrong number only for a partially-discounted bonus product (percentage-off "choice of bonus"), where `price` is nonzero.

The upstream tests do not constrain this at all: across the entire describe block (`cart.test.js:1643-1990`) the string `price` appears **zero** times. No fixture even has a price field. So there is no upstream contract you'd be breaking by changing the behaviour, and no upstream test that would catch a regression.

## 5. `itemId` and `bonusDiscountLineItemId`

- **`itemId`**: preserved, from the **first line only**. Not regenerated, not cleared. The merged object claims line₀'s `itemId` while carrying the summed quantity of N lines — so it is no longer a valid handle for a quantity-update or remove mutation. Upstream documents this deliberately: `cart.test.js:1966` — `test('itemId is not used in consolidation logic (only for display keys)')`, asserting at :1990 `expect(result[0].quantity).toBe(3) // Consolidated despite different itemIds`. Both call sites treat it as a React key only (`order-summary/index.jsx:88`, `order-detail.jsx:79` uses `index`).
- **`bonusDiscountLineItemId`**: preserved from the **first line only** — all other merged lines' IDs are **silently dropped**. `cart.test.js:1817` asserts `expect(result[0].bonusDiscountLineItemId).toBe('bonus-123')` but only in a case where both merged lines already had `'bonus-123'`. The test at `cart.test.js:1682-1713` merges `'bonus-123'`, `'bonus-123'` and `'bonus-456'` into one item and **never asserts the resulting `bonusDiscountLineItemId`** — the `'bonus-456'` loss is real and untested.

---

## House convention: every real read of these fields

### `price` / `priceAfterItemDiscount` → LINE TOTAL

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price.jsx:43,52,59`** — base reads `{price, priceAfterItemDiscount}`, assigns `currentPrice: priceAfterItemDiscount`, and at `:139-144` passes it to `DisplayPrice` with **no `quantity` prop**. Implies line total: base wants the already-multiplied number rendered as-is.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/index.jsx:35,43,56`** — `quantity = 1` default, then `price={currentPrice * quantity}` and `price={listPrice * quantity}`. Implies `DisplayPrice`'s own contract is **unit price in, caller opts into multiplication**. This is the crux of the mismatch: base feeds it a line total and relies on the `quantity=1` default to make the double-count a no-op.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-shipping-options.jsx:316`** — `shippingItem?.priceAfterItemDiscount || 0`. No signal: a shipping item is always quantity 1.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/partials/pickup-address.jsx:393`** — PropTypes declaration only, no read.

### `pricePerUnit` → UNIT price (base's own admission)

- **`item-price.jsx:55`** — `pricePerUnit: variant?.pricePerUnit` into `priceData`.
- **`item-price.jsx:77-78` and `:98-99`** — `{!isDesktop && variant?.quantity > 1 && !isASet && priceData?.pricePerUnit && (<PricePerItem currency={currency} basePrice={priceData.pricePerUnit} />)}`. Gated on **`quantity > 1`**. This is upstream stating outright that the main price element is *not* per-unit — otherwise a separate "ea" element gated on quantity > 1 would be redundant.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:158`** — `pricePerUnit: product?.pricePerUnit` in `getPriceData`, the wishlist/PDP (non-basket) path.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/index.jsx:84`** — PropTypes only.

### `basePrice` → UNIT price (authoritative)

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:6914`** (in the doc block for the `ProductItem` type declared at `:6968`): *"basePrice: The base price of the line item, which is the unit price not including adjustments."* This is the ground truth your `item-price.tsx:99` comment cites, and it checks out verbatim.
- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/multiship/multiship-order-summary.jsx:60`** — `price: pli.price || pli.basePrice || pli.itemTotal || undefined`. **Incoherent upstream bug**, useful as evidence: it treats a line total (`price`), a unit price (`basePrice`) and a line total (`itemTotal`) as interchangeable fallbacks for one display slot. Base is not internally consistent here, so don't treat base as a reliable convention authority.
- **`item-price.jsx:19,22,34`** — `PricePerItem`'s prop is *named* `basePrice` but is always fed `pricePerUnit`, never the actual `basePrice` field. Naming noise only.

### `priceAfterOrderDiscount` → read NOWHERE

Zero reads in `overrides/` or `retail-react-app/app/`. Every hit is a generated type declaration: `commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperBaskets/helpers.d.ts:83,148` and `commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperBasketsV2/helpers.d.ts:91,167,232,342,418,483,559,624`. No convention is established by usage — if you need it, you're the first.

---

## Division to get a per-unit price: this PR is the first

Single hit across `overrides/`, `retail-react-app/app/` and `commerce-sdk-react/`:

- **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-price.tsx:114`** — `currentPrice: priceAfterItemDiscount / unitQuantity`, with `const unitQuantity = quantity || 1;` at `:112`. Introduced by commit **98b0d609** `fix(cart): SFCC-11 cart item price shows the per-unit price, not price × quantity`.

Nearest other divisions, both unrelated to price:
- `retail-react-app/app/utils/bonus-product/cart.js:261` — `(totalPromotionCapacity / totalQualifyingQuantity) * (qualifyingItem.quantity || 1)`, promotion capacity allocation.
- `retail-react-app/app/components/product-view-modal/bundle.jsx:133` — `const quantityPerBundle = product.quantity / bundle.quantity`, quantity-per-bundle, not money.

So: dividing a money field by `quantity` is **not** an established pattern. This PR is the first instance.

---

## The collision you should care about

Your overridden `ItemPrice` is rendered from more than the cart drawer, and the two paths disagree on whether it receives a raw or consolidated line:

## 3. Exactly which numeric fields are summed / recomputed / carried over

The whole merge, `cart.js:78-98`:

```js
const aggregateBonusProductQuantities = (bonusItems) => {
    const productQuantityMap = new Map()

    bonusItems.forEach((item) => {
        const existingQuantity = productQuantityMap.get(item.productId) || 0
        productQuantityMap.set(item.productId, existingQuantity + (item.quantity || 0))
    })

    const result = []
    productQuantityMap.forEach((quantity, productId) => {
        const sampleItem = bonusItems.find((item) => item.productId === productId)
        if (sampleItem) {
            result.push({
                ...sampleItem,
                quantity: quantity
            })
        }
    })

    return result
}
```

`sampleItem` is `bonusItems.find(...)` — the **first** bonus line with that `productId`. The merged object is that first line spread wholesale, with exactly one key overwritten.

## 4. Is the merged `price` coherent with the merged `quantity`?

**No.** `quantity` becomes `Σ qᵢ` while `price` stays `line₀.price` (which, per the house convention below, is line₀'s *line total*, i.e. `unit × q₀`). So on a merged item:

```
price / quantity  ==  (unit × q₀) / Σqᵢ     ≠  unit
```

Two bonus lines of qty 1 at unit 100 merge to `{quantity: 2, price: 100}` → `price/quantity = 50`. Under-reports by a factor of N for N equal-quantity lines.

For a 100%-off bonus, `0 / anything === 0`, so the incoherence is latent. It becomes a real wrong number only for a partially-discounted bonus product (percentage-off "choice of bonus"), where `price` is nonzero.

Ordered by severity.

### 1. `variants` (+ `variants[].variationValues`, `variants[].orderable`, `variants[].productId`) — **hard crash**
`use-variation-attributes.js:75` is `return product.variants.filter(...)` — **no optional chaining**. It is called once per variation value from the `useMemo` at `:132-167`, which iterates `product.variationAttributes`. The projection selects `variationAttributes` but **not** `variants`, so for every cart line with variation attributes this throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')`, taking down the whole drawer render.

This is not speculative: the cart drawer renders today with a populated colour/size line (`item-attributes.tsx:31` cites real "Lilac Sand, One size" data), which means `variationAttributes` is non-empty today, which means that same unguarded line already executes today without throwing — so `variants` is present in today's response and the `select` string is what removes it.

Not in the projection. **[P]**-only (proven by the `ProductItem` type dump above and `cartItemMapper.ts:36-39`). Readers: `item-image.tsx:100` / base `:28`, `item-attributes.tsx:98` / base `:53`, `cartItemMapper.ts:95,122`, `use-variation-params.js:24,46`.

Two concrete regressions:
- **Image:** `findImageGroupBy` defaults `selectedVariationAttributes = {}` (`image-groups-utils.js:18`), reduces it to `{}` (`:38-45`), then `selectedIds.every(...)` on an empty array returns `true` (`:51`), so `.find` returns **the first small image group**. Combined with the PR's `allImages: true` — which is exactly the flag that makes SCAPI return the *whole* image model rather than only the requested variant's images — that means the first colour in the master's image model, not the shopper's colour. Note base's own cart pairs `allImages: true` with **no `select`** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:158-176`), i.e. `variationValues` present — that is the coherent combination this PR breaks.
- **Attributes:** `getDisplayVariationValues` defaults `values = {}` (`product-utils.js:25`) and returns `{}` (`:30-48`). The override renders `Object.values({}).join(', ')` → an **empty `<Text>`** (`item-attributes.tsx:149`), and `cartItemMapper.selectCombinedAttributes` returns `''` (`:123`). The Figma "Lilac Sand, One size" line disappears.

Minimal fix: add `variationValues` to the projection (preferred, matches base), **or** drop `allImages: true`.

### 3. `inventory.stockLevel`, `inventory.lowestStockLevelProductName`, `inventories[]` — inventory message goes permanently dead
Read at `use-derived-product.js:18-22,37,43,82-88`; rendered at `product-item/index.tsx:399-407`. Killed **twice over**: dropped from `expand` (no `availability`) *and* absent from the `select`. `stockLevel` falls to `0` (`:37`) → `isOutOfStock` true (`:72`) → but `showInventoryMessage` (`:122-124`) also needs `variant || type.bundle || type.item`, and all three collapse to falsy under this projection, so the net effect is silence rather than a false "Out of stock". Fragile-by-accident, not safe-by-design.

### 4. `c_maxOrderQuantity` — defeats the whole purpose of `maxOrderQuantity.ts`
Read at `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts:52`; drives the stepper `max` (`product-item/index.tsx:363`) and the "Maximum purchase quantity reached" message (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:304`). Not in the projection → permanently falls back to `3`. That file's docblock (`:19-23`) states the design intent explicitly: it "picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships, with no further frontend change needed". This projection silently removes that property.

### 5. `stepQuantity`
`use-derived-product.js:38`, `cartItemMapper.ts:139`. Falls to `1`. No visible impact in the cart drawer today (`ProductItem` destructures only `showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity` at `:293`, and `ZimmQuantityStepper` uses `min={1}`), but it is a genuine read that goes silently wrong.

### 6. `minOrderQuantity`
`use-derived-product.js:39-40`. Only matters when `quantity` is falsy, which the merge guarantees it isn't (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:276`). Low impact.

### 7. `type.item` and `type.variant`
The projection has `type.(bundle,master,set)` only. `type.item` is read at `use-derived-product.js:51` (feeds `isOutOfStock` `:72-77` and `showInventoryMessage` `:123`); `type.variant` at `use-variation-attributes.js:114` (only under `isProductPartOfBundle`, which is `false` here). **Add `item` and `variant` to `type.(...)` — it costs nothing.**

### 8. `imageGroups[viewType=swatch]`
`getVariantValueSwatch` (`use-variation-attributes.js:26-34`) requests `viewType: 'swatch'`; the `[viewType=small]` predicate strips it, so every decorated value's `image` becomes `undefined`. Latent only — nothing in the cart drawer renders those swatches (`ProductItem` never destructures `variationAttributes` from `useDerivedProduct`).

### 9. `pricePerUnit` — base-only
Base `item-price.jsx:55,77,98` reads it; the override deleted `PricePerItem` (`item-price.tsx:39-46`). Since every path in this repo resolves to the override, this is not a live break — but note it also needs the `prices` expand, so it is doubly removed.

### 10. Wishlist-branch price fields (not reachable from the cart drawer, but the same override is shared)
`getPriceData`/`findLowestPrice` (`product-utils.js:123-169,246-283`) read `hitType`, `variants[].price`, `productPromotions[].promotionalPrice`, `tieredPrices[].price/.quantity`, `priceMax`, `variants.length`. Only reached when `variant.itemId` is falsy (`item-price.tsx:94`), which never happens for a basket line. Safe **for this call site**; would break if this `select` were ever copied to the wishlist fetch.

---

# (c) Projection entries nothing reads (dead selection)

Genuinely dead:

1. **`variationAttributes.(... name ...)` — dead for the cart drawer specifically.** `getDisplayVariationValues` uses `attribute.name` as the object **key** (`product-utils.js:44`), and the cart's override throws the keys away: `Object.values(variationValues).join(', ')` (`item-attributes.tsx:149`, reached because `product-item/index.tsx:342` passes `combineAttributeValues`). The keys are only used on the non-combined path (`:156`), which base callers of the same component do use. **Keep it** unless you are certain no other surface renders labelled attributes — it is cheap.
2. **`imageGroups[...].variationAttributes.(id,values.(value))` — 100% dead *as configured*.** `findImageGroupBy` only touches these when `selectedVariationAttributes` is non-empty (`image-groups-utils.js:38-58`), and with `variationValues` missing it is always `{}`. So this sub-selection is paid for and never used. The fix is to add `variationValues`, not to remove this.
3. **`c_isSale` — selected but almost certainly unreachable.** Read at `item-image.tsx:108` / base `:35`. Custom attributes need the `custom_properties` expand in this codebase's own practice: `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:50` (`expand: ['promotions','variations','prices','images','custom_properties']`) and `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:318`. `expand: ['images','variations']` omits it, so `c_isSale` (and `c_maxOrderQuantity`) will not come back regardless of the `select`. Note also that `"custom_properties"` is **not** in the generated `expand` union (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:57374`), so adding it to a typed TS call site will need a cast — base gets away with it only because those files are `.jsx`.

Everything else in the projection is genuinely read: `id` (`item-name.tsx:74`, `item-attributes.tsx:131`, `product-item/index.tsx:320`), `name` (`item-name.tsx:79`, `item-price.tsx:140,150`, `cartItemMapper.ts:100,135`), `master.masterId` (`item-name.tsx:74`, `item-image.tsx:95`), `type.bundle` (`item-attributes.tsx:110,136`, `use-derived-product.js:36`), `type.master`/`type.set` (`item-price.tsx:88-89`), `variationAttributes.(id, values.(value))` (`product-utils.js:31,36`), `imageGroups[].viewType` (`image-groups-utils.js:22`), `images.(link,disBaseLink,alt)` (`item-image.tsx:147-148`).

---

# On `expand`

Removing `prices`, `promotions`, `availability`, `bundled_products`, `options`, `links` from the default set:

- **`prices` → removes `price`, `pricePerUnit`, `priceMax`, `priceRanges`, `prices`, `tieredPrices`.** Safe for the cart drawer: the merge re-asserts `price: item.price` **after** `...fullProduct` (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:275`), so the catalog `price` was already being discarded; `getPriceData`/`findLowestPrice` (the only `tieredPrices`/`priceMax` readers) are unreachable because `variant.itemId` is truthy (`item-price.tsx:94`); and the override deleted the only `pricePerUnit` reader. **But `perPricebook: true` (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:479`) becomes a dead parameter** — it exists to return the per-price-book `prices` map, which both the expand removal and the `select` drop. Remove it in the same PR or keep `prices`.
- **`promotions` → removes `productPromotions`.** Safe: the only reader is `findLowestPrice` (`product-utils.js:261`), unreachable as above. The promo pill in `item-attributes` uses basket `priceAdjustments[].promotionId` + a separate `usePromotions` call (`item-attributes.tsx:80,87-96`), untouched.
- **`availability` → removes `inventory`/`inventories`. NOT safe** — see (b)(3). Base's own precedent is instructive: the one place base uses a `select` at all, it pairs it with an expand that covers what it selects — `expand: ['availability','variations'], select: '(data.(id,inventory,inventories,master))'` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:196-197`, and identically at `pages/product-detail/index.jsx:173-174`).
- **`custom_properties` → never in the default set either, and needed for `c_isSale`/`c_maxOrderQuantity`.** See (c)(3).
- **`bundled_products` → removes `bundledProducts`.** Read at `item-attributes.tsx:182` — but only on the wishlist branch (`!productBundleIds`), and from that file's **own** `useProduct` call, not this fetch. No impact here.
- **`options`, `links`** — no readers found in this path.

## One unverified syntax risk

`imageGroups[viewType=small]` is an attribute-predicate filter. There is **no precedent for it anywhere in base retail-react-app 10.0.0 or this repo** — every existing `select` is plain parenthesis projection (`'(data.(id,inventory,inventories,master))'`, `pages/cart/index.jsx:197` and `pages/product-detail/index.jsx:174`), and the repo has zero occurrences of `imageGroups[` in any `select` (grep-confirmed). I could not verify from the codebase that SCAPI's `select` grammar accepts a value predicate rather than an index. Worth an actual live probe against the sandbox before merge — if the predicate is rejected, the endpoint will either 400 or silently return no image groups at all.

## Suggested minimal correction to the projection

```
(data.(id,name,master.(masterId),type.(bundle,item,master,set,variant),c_isSale,c_maxOrderQuantity,
 stepQuantity,minOrderQuantity,variationValues,variationAttributes.(id,name,values.(value,name)),

```
with `expand: ['images','variations','availability','custom_properties']`, and either drop `allImages: true` or keep it now that `variationValues` is back. `variants` is non-negotiable while `variationAttributes` is selected — `use-variation-attributes.js:75` gives you no choice.</result>

## Mechanism note (affects how to read all of this)

`package.json:17-20` sets `ccExtensibility: {extends: "@salesforce/retail-react-app", overridesDir: "overrides"}`. Any file at `overrides/app/<path>` shadows `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/<path>`. Relevant consequences:

- `overrides/app/utils/url.ts` fully shadows the base `app/utils/url.js` and re-implements `productUrlBuilder`, `rebuildPathWithParams`, `updateSearchParams` itself (`overrides/app/utils/url.ts:60`, `:73`, `:199`).
- `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/*` all shadow their base counterparts.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx` is **not** shadowed, and still renders base `ProductTile`.

# QUESTION 1 — `?color=` presence on inbound PDP links

- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:98` — identical bare path.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:35-46` / `overrides/app/utils/url.ts:60` — `rebuildPathWithParams` is the only thing that adds params, and only if a caller passes them. `updateSearchParams` (`url.js:48-57`) **deletes** a key when its value is falsy, so a `rebuildPathWithParams(url, {color: undefined})` produces **no** `color=`.

# QUESTION 2 — how `urlColour` is derived

**`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:324`:**

```ts
const urlColour = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get(SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID) ?? undefined;
```

- `location` is `useLocation()` (`:131`, `:223`).
- `SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID` is `'color'` (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:164`).
- The expression is **purely the URL read**. There is **no** fallback to a default or first-offered colour in the value of `urlColour` itself.

Two separate, distinct fallbacks exist elsewhere:

1. **Display-only fallback at the render site** — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1263`: `selectedValue={urlColour ?? attr.selectedValue?.value}`. Plus `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own internal fallback: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:96` — `const effectiveSelectedValue = offered.some((v) => v.value === selectedValue) ? selectedValue : offered[0]?.value;`. Neither changes `urlColour`.

2. **A URL-writing effect that makes `urlColour` non-falsy shortly after mount** — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:413-431`:
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (urlColour) return;
  if (product?.id !== requestedProductId) return;
  const colourAttr = product?.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
  const defaultColourValue = (colourAttr?.values as SfccSwatchAttrValue[] | undefined)?.find(
    (v) => v.orderable !== false,
  )?.value;
  if (!defaultColourValue) return;
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  params.set(SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID, defaultColourValue);
  history.replace(`${location.pathname}?${params.toString()}`);
}, [urlColour, product, requestedProductId]);
```
So on a `?color=`-less arrival, `urlColour` is `undefined` for the first render(s) — until `product.id === requestedProductId` and a first orderable colour value exists — then a `history.replace` writes `?color=<first orderable>` and `urlColour` becomes truthy on the next render. It stays `undefined` forever if `defaultColourValue` is falsy (`:427`).

Also consumed at `:459` and `:464` by `selectVariantScopedPriceData` (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/variantScopedPrice.ts:92`, `:113-117`).

# QUESTION 3 — colour swatch navigation mechanism

## Component location

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:74` (`ZimmColourSwatchGroup`), atom at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:71` (`ZimmColourSwatch`).

Two call sites:
1. PDP main sidebar — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1257`
2. Gallery overlay "Also available in" — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:218`

## How swatch `href` values are generated

### (a) PDP main sidebar — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1221-1235`

```ts
const values = (attr.values ?? []).map((v: SfccSwatchAttrValue) => {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  params.delete('pid');
  params.set(SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID, v.value ?? '');
  return {
    value: v.value ?? '',
    name: v.name ?? v.value ?? '',
    imageUrl: v.image?.disBaseLink || v.image?.link,
    href: `${location.pathname}?${params.toString()}`,
    orderable: v.orderable ?? true,
  };
});
```

**Param handling:** same pathname; **`pid` is explicitly deleted** (`:1226`, rationale at `:1223-1225`); `color` is set; **every other existing param — including `size` — is preserved verbatim.**

Note: the Zimmermann size selector does *not* write `size` into the URL — `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:465-483` keeps the picked size in local `localSizeValue` state (comment at `:466-468`: "size must not change the URL"), and `setLocalSizeValue` is called only at `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:1290`. So a `size=` param is normally absent; if it is present (e.g. a base-built deep link), it survives the colour swap.

### (b) Related-colour swatches (SFCC-708), appended to the same group — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1243-1252` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts:239-251`

```ts
href: `${urlBuilder({ id: item.masterProductID })}?${colourAttrId}=${encodeURIComponent(item.colourValue)}`,
orderable: true as const,
forceReload: true as const,
```
`urlBuilder` = `(params) => buildHref(productUrlBuilder(params))` (`index.tsx:1249`). This is a **fresh** URL: it **drops every existing param**, including `pid` and `size`.

<result>All claims verified from source. Here are the findings.

## Ground truth established first

`ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem` (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts:6968`, docs at `:6910-6966`):

| field | meaning | unit or line? |
|---|---|---|
| `basePrice` | "the **unit price** not including adjustments" (`:6914`) | **unit** |
| `price` | "price of the **line item** before applying any adjustments" (`:6935`) | **line total** |
| `priceAfterItemDiscount` | "price of the product **line item** including item-level adjustments" | **line total** |
| `priceAfterOrderDiscount` | "…including item-level adjustments and prorated order-level adjustments" | **line total** |
| `pricePerUnit` | **not a member of `ProductItem` at all** | — |

Corroborated by fixture `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/mocks/mock-data.js:37-55`: `basePrice: 9.59`, `quantity: 2`, `price: 19.18`, `priceAfterItemDiscount: 19.18`, `priceAfterOrderDiscount: 19.18`. So `price === basePrice × quantity`, and "adjustments" means `priceAdjustments` (promotions) only.

`pricePerUnit` exists only on Shopper **Products** `Product` (`:32760`, field `:32782`), documented "The price per unit if defined for the product", and fixtures show it equals the product's current unit price (`standard-product.js:78-79` `price: 4, pricePerUnit: 4`; `product-bundle.js:200-201` `price: 54.99, pricePerUnit: 54.99`).

---

## Findings

**1. `item-price.tsx:61-78` — order-level discounts are rendered as a per-line "Was/Now" markdown, and the same discount is then subtracted again in the Subtotal block.** 

`effectiveCurrentPrice = priceAfterOrderDiscount ?? …`, `isOnSale = price > effectiveCurrentPrice`, `listPrice = isOnSale ? price : null`.

Inputs: 1 unit @ $1000, no item promo, VIC 20% order promo. SCAPI returns `price: 1000`, `priceAfterItemDiscount: 1000`, `priceAfterOrderDiscount: 800`, `productSubTotal: 1000`, `orderPriceAdjustments: [{itemText:'VIC 20%', price:-200}]`.

Output, all inside one panel: line item reads **"Was $1,000.00 Now $800.00"** (`item-price.tsx:104-108`); Subtotal reads **$1,000.00** (`order-summary/index.tsx:218`); then **"VIC 20% Applied −$200.00"** (`:226-248`). The line item claims $800 while the Subtotal directly below claims $1,000, and the discount is visually applied twice. Base avoided this precisely by using `priceAfterItemDiscount`, which reconciles exactly with `productSubTotal` — "including item-level adjustments, but **not** including order-level adjustments" (`index.cjs.d.ts:7040`).

Requirements angle: PRC-09 (`.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md:35`) asks for "Original list price displayed alongside active sale price" — a markdown concept. PRC-18 (`:73`) treats customer-group discounts as a separate mechanism that explicitly does not stack with sale. Rendering a member discount as a strikethrough conflates the two. **Confidence: high** on the mechanism and the arithmetic; the product call on whether that's wanted is yours.

**2. `item-price.tsx:62,70` — the one case PRC-09 actually asks for, a sale/markdown pricebook, still gets no Was/Now.**

`price` is the *pricebook-resolved* line price, so for a markdown with no promotion attached, `price === priceAfterItemDiscount === priceAfterOrderDiscount` → `isOnSale` false → `listPrice: null` → no strikethrough. PRC-01 (`:15`) states the original/RRP arrives as a *separate additional price field* — which is exactly what the base comment it deletes ("listPrice is not available via basket pricing") meant. The override reverses that comment without making `listPrice` available; it substitutes "pre-promotion line price", a different quantity. Net effect: Was/Now fires for promotions (where PRC-18's model says it shouldn't) and stays silent for markdowns (where PRC-09 says it should). Contrast `getPriceData` (`product-utils.js:139-144`), which derives a genuine `listPrice` from `tieredPrices` — product data the basket doesn't carry, and which this PR's projection also drops. **Confidence: high.**

**3. `item-price.tsx:74` — the per-unit division is unnecessary for the pre-discount case and lossy for the post-discount case.**

`basePrice` is already the unit price, on the basket item, no division needed — base's own `PricePerItem` prop is even *named* `basePrice` (`item-price.jsx:19,22,34`) while being fed `pricePerUnit`. For a *post*-order-discount unit price there is no SCAPI field, so division is the only route, but it doesn't round-trip: qty 3, `price: 100.00`, 20% order discount → `priceAfterOrderDiscount: 80.00` → `80/3 = 26.6666…` → renders **"$26.67ea"** beside **"Now $80.00"**; 3 × 26.67 = 80.01. PRC-49 (`:55`) specifies rounding applied at line-item level. **Confidence: high.**

**4. `item-price.tsx:71-73` and `item-price.test.tsx:190-192,199-200` — the claim "SFCC computes `pricePerUnit` from the original list price" is unsupported, and I could find no evidence for it.**

Asked to settle this from source: I cannot substantiate it, and the evidence runs the other way. `pricePerUnit` is absent from `ProductItem` entirely; in order-summary base's `variant?.pricePerUnit` resolved from the merged **product**, where it is the current pricebook unit price (fixtures above), not a list price. The underlying concern — that it doesn't reflect basket-level discounts — is legitimate; the stated mechanism is not. The test makes the claim self-proving by inventing `pricePerUnit: 150` (= 300/2) in its fixture, a value real SFCC would not produce for that shape, so the test passes without testing anything about real data. Separately, the new projection omits `pricePerUnit`, so it wouldn't be present regardless. **Confidence: high** (scope: full grep of `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/*.d.ts`, `retail-react-app/app/`, and `overrides/` at PR head).

**5. `order-summary/index.tsx:81` — `variationValues` is missing from the `select:` projection, so checkout order-summary thumbnails show the wrong colour and the colour/size line renders empty. This ships live.**

`showCartItems={true}` is passed by base `pages/checkout/index.jsx:253` and `pages/checkout-one-click/index.jsx:605`, and no override intercepts either at PR head — so this is the checkout sidebar, not a dormant path.

`item-image.jsx:26-29` passes `selectedVariationAttributes: variant?.variationValues`; `item-attributes.jsx:51-54` passes the same into `getDisplayVariationValues`. `variationValues` is a product field (absent from `ProductItem`) and is not selected. Then:
- `findImageGroupBy` (`image-groups-utils.js:17-61`): default `{}` at `:18`, reduces to `{}` at `:38-45`, and at `:49-51` `[].every(...)` returns `true`, so `.find` returns the **first** small image group unconditionally → first colour's image for every line.
- `getDisplayVariationValues` (`product-utils.js:25-48`): `values = {}` → returns `{}` → attribute line renders nothing.

This also refutes the PR's own comments at `order-summary/index.tsx:71-73` and `:79-80` ("still lets `findImageGroupBy` match the purchased variant's colour") — what was removed is the *selection* side, not the image side, and `allImages: true` makes it worse by returning every colour's group for the first to win. **Confidence: high.**

**6. `order-summary/index.tsx:81` — `c_isSale` is selected but `expand` omits `custom_properties`, so the Sale badge silently stops rendering.** `item-image.jsx:38` reads `variant.c_isSale`. This repo's own precedent for custom attributes is explicit: `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:50` and `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:314` both include `'custom_properties'` in `expand`. Base's practice is that `expand` must cover `select` (`pages/cart/index.jsx:196-197`, `pages/product-detail/index.jsx:173-174`). **Confidence: medium-high** — repo/base precedent only, no live SCAPI probe.

**7. `order-summary/index.tsx:81` — the `imageGroups[viewType=small]` value predicate has no precedent I can find, and I could not verify SCAPI accepts it.** Every other `select` in the base package is plain parenthesis projection (`pages/cart/index.jsx:197`, `pages/product-detail/index.jsx:174`); zero occurrences of a bracket predicate in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` or in `overrides/` at PR head. If the grammar rejects it, the call either 400s or returns no image groups at all. Needs a dev-org probe before merge. **Confidence: the absence of precedent is certain; the syntax validity is undetermined.**

**8. `order-summary/index.tsx:115-117` → `item-price.tsx:74` — merged bonus lines break the division (answering Q7: no, they are not coherent).** `aggregateBonusProductQuantities` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/bonus-product/cart.js:78-98`, called from `:564`) spreads the **first** matching line and overwrites only `quantity` with the sum; `price`, `priceAfterItemDiscount` and `priceAfterOrderDiscount` all remain line₀'s. Inputs: two bonus lines, same `productId`, qty 1 each, partially discounted to $100 line each → merged `{quantity: 2, priceAfterOrderDiscount: 100}` → "ea" renders **$50.00** instead of $100.00, under-reporting by a factor of N. Latent for the canonical 100%-off bonus, whose money fields are all zero (`mock-data.js:5739-5757`), real for a percentage-off "choice of bonus". `isOnSale`/Was/Now stay coherent (both sides line₀'s); only the division is wrong. **Confidence: medium-high** — no partially-discounted bonus fixture exists to confirm against.

**9. `item-price.tsx:100-108` — the on-sale branch bypasses `DisplayPrice`, dropping set handling, `isRange`, and the a11y label.** `DisplayPrice` returns current-price-only with no list price for a set (`display-price/index.jsx:68-70`); the override renders Was/Now instead. `isRange` is computed at `item-price.tsx:77` and unused on that path. And `labelForA11y={variant?.name}` is passed to both `DisplayPrice` branches but not to `ZimmProductPrice`, whose docblock (`zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:126-134`) states it deliberately renders no a11y-name node — so on a discounted line a screen reader hears "Was $600.00 Now $480.00" with no product name, in a list of several items. Project targets WCAG 2.2 AA. **Confidence: high on the code path; low on frequency** — basket lines are SKUs so `type.master` should be false; the set case is the plausible one.

**10. The changed data flow has no test or story coverage.** `order-summary/index.test.tsx` never sets `showCartItems` and mocks out `item-name`/`item-attributes`; `index.stories.tsx` has no `showCartItems` story. So the `select:` projection, the `useProducts` merge and the `item-price` integration — the riskiest parts — are untested. `item-price.test.tsx` covers only branch selection, against hand-built fixtures, with no assertion that the main figure is a line total while "ea" is a unit. **Confidence: high** (read both files at PR head in full).

---

## What I could not determine

- **Whether `priceAfterOrderDiscount` is always present.** Typed optional; the single `productItem` fixture has it. So `?? priceAfterItemDiscount` may be dead for baskets — and I can't speak for **order** responses, which also render this component (`pages/account/order-detail.jsx:34`, `pages/confirmation/index.jsx:47`). Untested either way.
- **SCAPI's `select` predicate grammar** (finding 7) and **whether `c_*` strictly requires `custom_properties`** (finding 6) — both need a live probe.
- **Whether finding 1 is a deliberate product decision.** `item-price.test.tsx:2` cites SFCC-645/SFCC-778; I did not read those tickets. If either asks for order-level discounts as Was/Now, finding 1 becomes a PRC-09/PRC-18 doc conflict to resolve rather than a defect.
- **Gift cards** — SCAPI puts gift certificates in `giftCertificateItems`, not `productItems`, so they never reach this component; I did not verify Zimmermann's GiveX cards aren't modelled as ordinary products. Zero-price and `quantity: 0` are both benign (`0 ?? 1 = 0` → `quantity > 0` false → falls back to `effectiveCurrentPrice`, and the `quantity > 1` guard suppresses the "ea" line).
- **I did not re-run any gate** — none of the above rests on a gate number. Worth noting the lint delta you measured (+524 problems for ~1050 added lines) is consistent with the new files mixing indent/semicolon styles (`item-price.tsx` and `order-summary/index.tsx` use 4-space no-semicolon; both test files use 2-space with semicolons) — but that is outside my angle and I did not verify it.

One process caveat: two helper searches I ran returned partly from the working tree (the other branch), which has its own `item-variant` overrides and a `cartDrawerContainer`. I discarded those portions and re-verified every load-bearing claim above directly against `git show 1a32bc94:` or the base package.</result>

cat >> ~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-645/review-pr118.md <<'EOF'

## ADDED after live verification against the PR's own preview deployment

12. **IN-SCOPE / CONFIRMED / BLOCKER** — order-summary/index.tsx:81 — the new `select:` projection is **invalid SCAPI selector grammar and returns HTTP 400**. The `imageGroups[viewType=small]` bracket predicate is the malformed part. Verified three ways:
    - Replayed the exact shipped params against the live SCAPI proxy: `400 Malformed Selector`. Same 400 with the brackets percent-encoded AND raw, so it is not an encoding artifact of my test.
    - Bisected: dropping only `[viewType=small]` returns `200 OK`. Every other clause in the string is valid on its own.
    - Reproduced on the real deployed preview at /checkout with an item in the basket: `HTTP 400 ... select=(data.(id,name,master.(masterId),...imageGroups[viewType=smal...`
    User-visible effect on the checkout order summary cart-items panel, measured from the live DOM:
    - `imgs: []` — **no product thumbnail renders at all**
    - attributes line renders only `Quantity: 1`; the colour and size values are gone (they come from the product `variationValues`/`variationAttributes`, which never arrive)
    - the item name survives only because the basket ProductItem carries `productName` and `item-name` falls back to it
    Surface: base `pages/checkout/index.jsx:253` and `pages/checkout-one-click/index.jsx:605` are the only callers passing `showCartItems={true}`, and neither is overridden at head — so this is the live checkout sidebar. The cart page renders OrderSummary without `showCartItems`, so `CartItems` never mounts there and the cart page is unaffected.
    The 400 is swallowed with no error surfaced, which also cuts against AGENTS.md > Graceful Degradation ("surface an explicit error instead").
    Origin: commit 18bcfa30 "scope order-summary product query to needed fields", added in response to a CodeRabbit performance suggestion that was then marked resolved. — state: pending adjudication — THIS IS THE BLOCKER

13. **IN-SCOPE / CONFIRMED (mechanism) / PLAUSIBLE (price impact)** — product-detail/index.tsx:497-511 vs product-view/index.tsx:469 — the colour+size guard treats a *live* size selection as stale. Browser-verified on two products on the preview: after picking a size and then switching colour, `ProductView`'s size trigger **still displays the previously chosen size** (8481DF261 BLK→CHT: trigger stays "0P"; 25519318M JJ8UTXX→JJ169XX→back: trigger stays "XS"). `localSizeValue` is never reset on colour change. So `selectedSizeSelection.colour !== urlColour` fires and `pricingVariantId` falls back to `urlPid` (undefined) → colour-range pricing → Was/Now suppressed, while the UI shows a complete colour+size selection. CodeRabbit raised this shape at product-detail/index.tsx:501 and **withdrew it** on the reasoning that "ProductView retains that local size selection across colour navigation, so the finding's claim was incorrect" — retention is precisely what makes the guard wrong, so the withdrawal inverted the problem rather than dissolving it. PLAUSIBLE on price impact only: I could not find a product on this environment that is both multi-colour and has per-size sale pricing, so I proved the state desync but not a wrong number on screen. — state: pending adjudication

14. **OUT-OF-SCOPE / CONFIRMED** — item-price.tsx:61-74 — `price` is the LINE TOTAL pre-adjustment and `priceAfterOrderDiscount` is the line total including prorated order-level adjustments (commerce-sdk-isomorphic ProductItem docs). ## A. The a11y regression — confirmed, but not in the direction the brief assumes

**What `labelForA11y` actually produces.** `display-price/current-price.jsx:56-66` renders a second, hidden node: `<span class="chakra-visually-hidden" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">{labelForA11y}{"current price $X"}</span>`. `list-price.jsx:55-61` does the same with `"original price $Y"` (`messages.js:17-28`). **Before vs after, for a discounted cart line:**

- **Base** (`item-price.jsx:51-56`) sets `listPrice: null` *unconditionally* — so base never showed a strikethrough in the cart at all. A screen reader heard: `"current price $595.00"` then `"Silk Midi Dresscurrent price $595.00"` (name and label concatenated with no separator — a base wart).

So it is **better in one respect** (the original price is now announced at all) and **worse in two** (name gone, semantic price labels gone). That changes the fix from "revert" to "add the name back".

**Is the name associated any other way? No — search scope stated.** I had an agent grep for `aria-labelledby|aria-describedby|role="group"|<li|as="li"|htmlFor|id=` across `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/*`, `product-item/index.jsx`, `product-item-list/index.jsx`, and all 8 call sites, plus all of `overrides/`. In base `product-item/index.jsx:54-131` the only such attribute in the entire file is `data-testid` on line 57. `item-name.jsx:22-27` emits `<h2><a>NAME</a></h2>` with **no `id`**. The price sits three roleless `<div>`s over in a cousin subtree — no shared accessible-name scope exists. `ItemPrice` spreads `{...props}`, so a caller *could* inject `aria-labelledby`; I checked all 8 call sites and none passes any `aria-*`.

**Blast radius is 8 surfaces, not just the cart** — every one imports the base specifier, so all receive the override: base `product-item/index.jsx:19` (cart page + wishlist), `order-summary/index.jsx:30`, `multiship/multiship-order-summary.jsx:22`, `pages/confirmation/index.jsx:47`, `checkout/partials/shipping-product-cards.jsx:18`, `checkout/partials/pickup-address.jsx:29`, `account/order-detail.jsx:34`, and the PR's own `overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.tsx:29`.

---

## B. Live regions — the count is unchanged; the content is what broke

**Correction to the brief's premise, both halves:**

1. **All five `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` in `order-summary/index.tsx` (lines 207, 229, 250, 316, 348) are inherited verbatim** from base `order-summary/index.jsx` (lines 160, 180, 194, 248, 280). Not new. Nothing to raise there.
2. **N discounted items do not add N *new* live regions.** Base `DisplayPrice` already put one `aria-live` region on *every* cart line via that `VisuallyHidden` node. So it's 1 region per line before and 1 after.

What actually changed: the region **moved from a hidden sibling onto the visible price node** (`zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:94-96`, `:136`), and **lost its name prefix**.

**Mechanism on a basket mutation.** An order-level promotion is distributed across all line items, so changing *one* line's quantity mutates `priceAfterOrderDiscount` on *every* line. Each discounted line's `<p>` text changes → `aria-atomic="true"` re-reads the whole thing → N polite announcements queue up as `"Was $795.00 Now $595.00"`, `"Was $450.00 Now $337.50"`, … with **nothing identifying which line each belongs to**, plus the 5 inherited summary rows if the summary is on screen. Base was equally noisy but each announcement was self-identifying. **The name prefix was the only disambiguator, and that is precisely what was dropped** — so the regression is in B, not just A.

Two mechanism details worth having: removing an item unmounts its `ItemVariantProvider` (keyed `order-summary-item-{productId}-{itemId}`, line 126-128), and a *removed* or *newly inserted* live region announces nothing — so "remove item" announces only the surviving lines' discount redistribution. And base `product-item/index.jsx` renders `CartItemVariantPrice` **twice** (`:71` `HideOnDesktop`, `:104` `HideOnMobile`); `responsive/index.jsx:16-34` hides via `display: none`, which removes from the a11y tree — so one active region per line, not two.

---

**Actual resolved values.** `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:24` sets `textStyle: 'price'` in `baseStyle.container`, which is the *same* for PDP and cart. `typography.ts:204-210` resolves it to:

| | value |
|---|---|
| `fontSize` | `fontSizes['2xs']` = **`0.875rem` (14px)** |
| `lineHeight` | `lineHeights['2xs']` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** |
| `fontWeight` | `fontWeights.medium` = **500** |
| `letterSpacing` | `letterSpacings.sm` = **`0`** |
| `sale` `gap` | `var(--zimm-scale-xs)` = **`0.5rem` (8px)** |
| `sale` `minHeight` | `var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** |
| `sale.wasPrice` colour | `text.muted` = `grey[300]` = **`#969696`** (~2.9:1 on white) |
| `sale.nowPrice` colour | `status.success` = `green[500]` = **`#2d5a3d`** (~8:1 on white) |

**So it does *not* render at "PDP scale" in the sense of being too big — it renders too small.** The base cart price is `<Text as="b">` with no `fontSize`, inheriting body size; `theme/index.ts:60` replaces `styles.global` wholesale with `globalStyles`, which sets no `body` `fontSize`, so that inherits the 16px browser root — bold (~700). The new price is **14px / weight 500**. Net effect: **on the same cart page, a discounted line's price is smaller and lighter than a non-discounted line's, and green rather than black**, because the two go through different components. That's the visual finding, and it needs designer input, not a code guess.

Also: `wasPrice`'s sub-AA `#969696` was signed off in `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:38-41` as *"a considered call by the FE lead to match the design system"* — scoped to the PDP. This PR silently extends that exception to cart, checkout order summary, confirmation and order history without re-approval, against AGENTS.md's WCAG 2.2 AA target.

**Translation ids — yes, a real problem.** `product_view.label.was_price` / `product_view.label.now_price` appear in **0 files** across `translations/` and `overrides/app/static/translations/` (that's my full search scope). ## B. Live regions — the count is unchanged; the content is what broke

**Correction to the brief's premise, both halves:**

1. **All five `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` in `order-summary/index.tsx` (lines 207, 229, 250, 316, 348) are inherited verbatim** from base `order-summary/index.jsx` (lines 160, 180, 194, 248, 280). Not new. Nothing to raise there.
2. **N discounted items do not add N *new* live regions.** Base `DisplayPrice` already put one `aria-live` region on *every* cart line via that `VisuallyHidden` node. So it's 1 region per line before and 1 after.

What actually changed: the region **moved from a hidden sibling onto the visible price node** (`zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:94-96`, `:136`), and **lost its name prefix**.

**Mechanism on a basket mutation.** An order-level promotion is distributed across all line items, so changing *one* line's quantity mutates `priceAfterOrderDiscount` on *every* line. Each discounted line's `<p>` text changes → `aria-atomic="true"` re-reads the whole thing → N polite announcements queue up as `"Was $795.00 Now $595.00"`, `"Was $450.00 Now $337.50"`, … with **nothing identifying which line each belongs to**, plus the 5 inherited summary rows if the summary is on screen. Base was equally noisy but each announcement was self-identifying. **The name prefix was the only disambiguator, and that is precisely what was dropped** — so the regression is in B, not just A.

Two mechanism details worth having: removing an item unmounts its `ItemVariantProvider` (keyed `order-summary-item-{productId}-{itemId}`, line 126-128), and a *removed* or *newly inserted* live region announces nothing — so "remove item" announces only the surviving lines' discount redistribution. | | value |

| `fontSize` | `fontSizes['2xs']` = **`0.875rem` (14px)** |
| `lineHeight` | `lineHeights['2xs']` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** |
| `fontWeight` | `fontWeights.medium` = **500** |
| `letterSpacing` | `letterSpacings.sm` = **`0`** |

| `sale` `minHeight` | `var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** |

## B. Live regions — the count is unchanged; the content is what broke

**Correction to the brief's premise, both halves:**

1. **All five `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` in `order-summary/index.tsx` (lines 207, 229, 250, 316, 348) are inherited verbatim** from base `order-summary/index.jsx` (lines 160, 180, 194, 248, 280). Not new. Nothing to raise there.
2. **N discounted items do not add N *new* live regions.** Base `DisplayPrice` already put one `aria-live` region on *every* cart line via that `VisuallyHidden` node. So it's 1 region per line before and 1 after.

What actually changed: the region **moved from a hidden sibling onto the visible price node** (`zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:94-96`, `:136`), and **lost its name prefix**.

**Mechanism on a basket mutation.** An order-level promotion is distributed across all line items, so changing *one* line's quantity mutates `priceAfterOrderDiscount` on *every* line. Each discounted line's `<p>` text changes → `aria-atomic="true"` re-reads the whole thing → N polite announcements queue up as `"Was $795.00 Now $595.00"`, `"Was $450.00 Now $337.50"`, … with **nothing identifying which line each belongs to**, plus the 5 inherited summary rows if the summary is on screen. Base was equally noisy but each announcement was self-identifying. **The name prefix was the only disambiguator, and that is precisely what was dropped** — so the regression is in B, not just A.

Two mechanism details worth having: removing an item unmounts its `ItemVariantProvider` (keyed `order-summary-item-{productId}-{itemId}`, line 126-128), and a *removed* or *newly inserted* live region announces nothing — so "remove item" announces only the surviving lines' discount redistribution. And base `product-item/index.jsx` renders `CartItemVariantPrice` **twice** (`:71` `HideOnDesktop`, `:104` `HideOnMobile`); `responsive/index.jsx:16-34` hides via `display: none`, which removes from the a11y tree — so one active region per line, not two.

| `lineHeight` | `lineHeights['2xs']` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** |
| `fontWeight` | `fontWeights.medium` = **500** |
| `letterSpacing` | `letterSpacings.sm` = **`0`** |
