The price sits three roleless `<div>`s over in a cousin subtree — no shared accessible-name scope exists. `ItemPrice` spreads `{...props}`, so a caller *could* inject `aria-labelledby`; I checked all 8 call sites and none passes any `aria-*`.

**Blast radius is 8 surfaces, not just the cart** — every one imports the base specifier, so all receive the override: base `product-item/index.jsx:19` (cart page + wishlist), `order-summary/index.jsx:30`, `multiship/multiship-order-summary.jsx:22`, `pages/confirmation/index.jsx:47`, `checkout/partials/shipping-product-cards.jsx:18`, `checkout/partials/pickup-address.jsx:29`, `account/order-detail.jsx:34`, and the PR's own `overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.tsx:29`.

---

## B. Live regions — the count is unchanged; the content is what broke

**Correction to the brief's premise, both halves:**

1. **All five `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` in `order-summary/index.tsx` (lines 207, 229, 250, 316, 348) are inherited verbatim** from base `order-summary/index.jsx` (lines 160, 180, 194, 248, 280). Not new. Nothing to raise there.
2. **N discounted items do not add N *new* live regions.** Base `DisplayPrice` already put one `aria-live` region on *every* cart line via that `VisuallyHidden` node. So it's 1 region per line before and 1 after.

What actually changed: the region **moved from a hidden sibling onto the visible price node** (`zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:94-96`, `:136`), and **lost its name prefix**.

**Mechanism on a basket mutation.** An order-level promotion is distributed across all line items, so changing *one* line's quantity mutates `priceAfterOrderDiscount` on *every* line. Each discounted line's `<p>` text changes → `aria-atomic="true"` re-reads the whole thing → N polite announcements queue up as `"Was $795.00 Now $595.00"`, `"Was $450.00 Now $337.50"`, … with **nothing identifying which line each belongs to**, plus the 5 inherited summary rows if the summary is on screen. Base was equally noisy but each announcement was self-identifying. **The name prefix was the only disambiguator, and that is precisely what was dropped** — so the regression is in B, not just A.

Two mechanism details worth having: removing an item unmounts its `ItemVariantProvider` (keyed `order-summary-item-{productId}-{itemId}`, line 126-128), and a *removed* or *newly inserted* live region announces nothing — so "remove item" announces only the surviving lines' discount redistribution. And base `product-item/index.jsx` renders `CartItemVariantPrice` **twice** (`:71` `HideOnDesktop`, `:104` `HideOnMobile`); `responsive/index.jsx:16-34` hides via `display: none`, which removes from the a11y tree — so one active region per line, not two.

---

## C. Type scale — the concern is real but *inverted*; the i18n concern is real as stated

**Actual resolved values.** `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:24` sets `textStyle: 'price'` in `baseStyle.container`, which is the *same* for PDP and cart. `typography.ts:204-210` resolves it to:

| | value |
|---|---|
| `fontSize` | `fontSizes['2xs']` = **`0.875rem` (14px)** |
| `lineHeight` | `lineHeights['2xs']` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** |
| `fontWeight` | `fontWeights.medium` = **500** |
| `letterSpacing` | `letterSpacings.sm` = **`0`** |
| `sale` `gap` | `var(--zimm-scale-xs)` = **`0.5rem` (8px)** |
| `sale` `minHeight` | `var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** |
| `sale.wasPrice` colour | `text.muted` = `grey[300]` = **`#969696`** (~2.9:1 on white) |
| `sale.nowPrice` colour | `status.success` = `green[500]` = **`#2d5a3d`** (~8:1 on white) |

**So it does *not* render at "PDP scale" in the sense of being too big — it renders too small.** The base cart price is `<Text as="b">` with no `fontSize`, inheriting body size; `theme/index.ts:60` replaces `styles.global` wholesale with `globalStyles`, which sets no `body` `fontSize`, so that inherits the 16px browser root — bold (~700). The new price is **14px / weight 500**. Net effect: **on the same cart page, a discounted line's price is smaller and lighter than a non-discounted line's, and green rather than black**, because the two go through different components. That's the visual finding, and it needs designer input, not a code guess.

Also: `wasPrice`'s sub-AA `#969696` was signed off in `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:38-41` as *"a considered call by the FE lead to match the design system"* — scoped to the PDP. This PR silently extends that exception to cart, checkout order summary, confirmation and order history without re-approval, against AGENTS.md's WCAG 2.2 AA target.

**Translation ids — yes, a real problem.** `product_view.label.was_price` / `product_view.label.now_price` appear in **0 files** across `translations/` and `overrides/app/static/translations/` (that's my full search scope). So every non-English storefront renders the English `defaultMessage`. Pre-existing on the PDP; this PR newly leaks untranslated "Was"/"Now" into cart, checkout summary, confirmation and order history across da-DK, de-DE, en-AE, en-CA, en-CH, en-GB, en-HK, en-US. Compounding it, the ids sit in the **`product_view.*` namespace**, so a translator working the cart/checkout copy batch will not find them — `translations/` is Tier 2, Integration/SI-owned (`protectedFiles.md`), so a component cannot fix its own namespace after the fact. Two *new* ids in this PR are also at 0 coverage: `order_summary.label.promotion_applied_suffix`, `order_summary.label.shipping_tbd` (by contrast the inherited `order_summary.label.promo_applied` is in 26 files and `tax_tbd` in 8 — which is what proves extraction has run for this namespace and simply hasn't for the new keys).

---

## D. The PDP selection state machine

Ground truth established first:

- `urlColour` (**head:335**) is purely `URLSearchParams(location.search).get('color')` — no fallback in the value itself.
- **head:424-442** is a backfill effect: if `urlColour` is falsy and `product.id === requestedProductId`, it `history.replace`s `?color=<first value with orderable !== false>`.
- Colour swatches are **client-side** — `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:11` `chakra(RouteLink)` used at `:137`. `<ProductView` at **head:1266 has no `key`**, `routes.tsx:76-78` matches on pathname only, so a search-param change **re-renders, never remounts**. (The `forceReload` `<chakra.a>` branch at `:109-131` is only taken by SFCC-708 cross-master related swatches.)
- The swatch href (**head:1275-1289**) deletes `pid` (`:1280`) and preserves every other param.
- **`localSizeValue` has exactly one writer and no reset.** `product-view/index.tsx:466` (declaration), `:1271` (the only `setLocalSizeValue` call). Search scope: all of `overrides/`, all of `e2e/`, and all of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` — zero other hits.
- The page's own `variant = useVariant(product)` (head:405) reads **URL** variation params, so it stays `undefined` while size lives only in local state — which is why the pid-sync effect at **head:539-549** does *not* fire on a size pick. **The PR's premise ("pid is NEVER written to the URL", head:318-319/449-451/477-478) is correct for a size pick specifically**, though the page *does* own a pid-writer 90 lines below and the comment doesn't say so.

**D1 — bare PDP URL, no `?color=`, then pick a size.** *Mostly correct, with one deterministic gap.*
This is the **common** entry path, not an edge case: the PLP grid (`productListCardMapper.ts:290` — `buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({id: hit.productId}))`), every recently-viewed surface, and every cart/checkout/wishlist line-item link all produce a bare `/product/<id>`. Only home/PDP Einstein rails (unshadowed base `ProductTile/index.jsx:133-139`) and PDP-internal swatches can supply one.
`urlColour` is falsy for the first render(s), then the backfill fires. The size dropdown needs the same `product` data the backfill gates on, so a human click cannot realistically land in the window — **low real risk.** But when `defaultColourValue` resolves falsy (line 438 `return`s), `urlColour` stays `undefined` **forever**: `handleVariationChange` (head:484) then discards *every* size pick, `pricingVariantId` returns `urlPid` (undefined), `selectVariantScopedPriceData` hits `variantScopedPrice.ts:118-119` → `null` → head:1326 `null ?? headerProps.priceData` falls back to master-range pricing. Graceful, not a crash — but Was/Now never narrows to the selected size. Two ways to reach it: a master with **no `color` variation attribute** (size-only), or one where every colour value is explicitly `orderable: false`.

**D2 — size M on colour A, switch to colour B.** *Incorrect UI/price disagreement.*
No remount → `localSizeValue` stays `'M'` → `effectiveControlledVariationValues` (product-view:468-479) rebuilds as `{color: B, size: 'M'}` → `effectiveSizeValue` = `'M'` → **the dropdown at `:1268` still displays M**. Colour navigation does not call `onVariationChange`, so `selectedSizeSelection` still holds `{colour: 'A', …}`. The guard at head:500 (`'A' === 'B'` → false) correctly zeroes `effectiveSize`; `urlPid` is undefined (swatch deleted it) → colour-range pricing. **Result: the UI claims a specific size is selected while the price silently reverts to colour-range treatment.** The guard does exactly what its comment says — the problem is the UI it's guarding against.

**D3 — switch back to colour A without touching the dropdown.** *Correct outcome, fragile mechanism.*
`selectedSizeSelection` is `{colour:'A', size:'M', productId}`, never reset (single writer, head:485). Both guards pass → `effectiveSize = 'M'` → `pricingVariantId` = the A/M variant → Was/Now shows, and the dropdown shows M. **UI and price agree.** But this is only correct *because `localSizeValue` is never reset*. If someone fixes that real ProductView bug, `selectedSizeSelection` keeps saying `M` while the dropdown shows nothing selected — a single-variant Was/Now for a size the shopper can't see chosen. **The PR's correctness here is load-bearing on an undocumented bug in another component**, and nothing records that coupling.
Same shape on product→product navigation (`path="/product/:productId"`, no remount): the `productId` guard (head:501) correctly rejects the stale size for *pricing*, while the dropdown still shows product A's size on product B. Credit due — that guard is genuinely necessary and correct.

**D4 — which `product` does the memo see?** *Correct, for a reason the PR doesn't state.*
On a size pick no `pid` is written, so `requestedProductId` stays the master and `product` is the **master** — `variants[]` populated, the `find` at head:505-509 works. Separately, a standalone-variant response *does* carry `variants[]`: base `isVariantValueOrderable` (`use-variation-attributes.js:74-82`) does `product.variants.filter(...)` completely unguarded and is called at `:162` on every render, so the base PDP would throw on every deep-linked variant page otherwise. (`variantScopedPrice.ts:62-64` cites "line 162" for the unguarded access — that's the *call site*; the access is in `isVariantValueOrderable`. Inference from base code, **not** live-API verified.) And when `product` *is* a non-master, `getPriceData` ignores injected variants entirely — `product-utils.js:257` uses `[product]` — so the price comes from the variant's own `tieredPrices`. Fallback is `match?.productId ?? urlPid` (head:510), which can be `undefined` → colour-range → Was/Now suppressed. No crash path.
**One unverified edge:** the `find` matches on colour+size only. A master with a **third** variation axis would have multiple matches and `find` silently takes the first, pricing the wrong SKU. Mechanism confirmed in source; I could not confirm whether such a product exists in the catalogue.

---

## Numbered findings

**1. `item-price.tsx:104-108` — product name dropped from the price announcement on 8 surfaces.**
Mechanism: the new `ZimmProductPrice` branch omits `labelForA11y`, which lines 111 and 118 still pass on both `DisplayPrice` branches. `display-price/current-price.jsx:56-66`'s `VisuallyHidden` node is the *only* construct joining name to price anywhere in the chain; nothing else in base `product-item/index.jsx:54-131` or any of the 8 callers does it (scope stated in §A).
Scenario: a screen-reader user tabs a 4-item cart with 2 discounted lines and hears `"Was $795.00 Now $595.00"` twice with nothing saying which garment. Undiscounted lines still announce their name — so it's inconsistent *within one cart*.
Severity: **Should-fix** (arguably blocking against AGENTS.md's WCAG 2.2 AA target). Confidence: **high**.

**2. `item-price.tsx:107` — `isLive={true}` in a repeated list, against the atom's own documented guidance and an in-repo precedent.**
Mechanism: `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:56-62` documents `isLive={false}` for exactly this case — *"when this atom is reused inside a grid of many cards … where the price never changes after mount"* — and `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:157` already applies it. Here the price *does* change (order-discount redistribution), so `false` isn't automatically right either — but `true` plus no name (finding 1) is the worst combination. The atom's docblock at `:127-131` justifies having no hidden name node on the premise that *"`currentPrice` arrives already formatted … by the page"* — true on a single-price PDP, false in a list of N.
Severity: **Should-fix**. Confidence: **high**.

**3. `order-summary/index.tsx:29` — base-path import of a component this same PR overrides; the new story and test silently exercise the base component.**
Mechanism: exactly the trap `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents under "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component". I verified both halves: `.storybook/main.js:32` aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`'s `alias` block has **no** entry for that package. Only the real app build runs `ccExtensibility` (`package.json` → `overridesDir: "overrides"`).
Scenario: `index.stories.tsx`'s four stories and `index.test.tsx`'s seven tests render base `item-price.jsx` — no Was/Now, no `ZimmProductPrice`, no live region. Anyone using them to sanity-check discount rendering gets a false negative. Fix: `'../item-variant/item-price'`. The sibling imports (`item-variant`, `item-image`, `item-name`, `item-attributes`, lines 25-28) have no override and are correctly left on the base path.
Severity: **Should-fix**. Confidence: **high** (config verified, not just the rule doc).

**4. `order-summary/index.tsx:218` and `:368` — `?? 0` fabricates a confident `$0.00` for an unknown total.**
Mechanism: `productSubTotal ?? 0` and `orderTotal ?? productTotal ?? 0`. Base had no fallback and rendered `NaN` (react-intl's `formatNumber` try/catches and returns `String(value)` — `@formatjs/intl/lib/src/number.js:36-45`), so this *is* an improvement over a crash-adjacent render, but `$0.00` reads as a real value where `NaN` reads as broken.
The same file gets this right two rows away — `:286-313` shows **TBD** for null `shippingTotal`, and `index.stories.tsx:106-107` states the principle explicitly: *"TBD, not a fabricated $0.00."* Applied to shipping and tax, not to subtotal or order total. Against AGENTS.md Graceful Degradation ("surface an explicit error instead").
Severity: **Should-fix**. Confidence: **high**.

**5. `product-detail/index.tsx:484` — size selections are silently discarded whenever `urlColour` never resolves.**
Mechanism and both trigger conditions in §D1. Not a race (that window is unreachable by a human) — a deterministic gap for size-only masters and all-unorderable-colour masters.
Severity: **Should-fix** if such products exist; **Nit** if they don't. Confidence: **high on mechanism, unverified on catalogue data** — I could not check live SFCC.

**6. `product-detail/index.tsx:497-511` + `product-view/index.tsx:466`/`:1268` — dropdown and price disagree after a colour switch (D2), and D3's correctness depends on an unreset `localSizeValue`.**
Mechanism in §D2/D3. Minimum viable fix is a comment on head:497 recording that `pricingVariantId`'s correctness assumes ProductView does *not* reset `localSizeValue` — so whoever fixes that bug knows to revisit this. The proper fix (reset on colour change, in both places, coherently) crosses into `product-view/index.tsx`, which per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 ("never refactor upward") is a separate ticket.
Severity: **Should-fix**. Confidence: **high** on D2/D3 traces; both fully source-verified.

**7. 516 `prettier/prettier` errors from three of the five new files — the converted files were never formatted.**
Breakdown I measured: `order-summary/index.tsx` **294**, `item-price.test.tsx` **117**, `item-price.tsx` **105**; `order-summary/index.stories.tsx` and `index.test.tsx` are **0**. The three offenders retain base SFCC formatting (4-space indent, no semicolons); the two clean files were hand-written. That contrast rules out a config problem and pins it to a missed `npx prettier --write` during the copy-first conversion. One command fixes it.
Severity: **Should-fix** (mechanical, but it's ~40% of the repo's total lint count from four files). Confidence: **high** — measured.

**8. `order-summary/index.tsx:389` — `basket.couponItems!` is a hard eslint error with no justifying comment.**
Mechanism: `@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion`, severity 2, verified. The `!` is needed because the guard at `:373` (`(basket.couponItems?.length ?? 0) > 0`) doesn't narrow the outer property — so it's runtime-safe but `.claude/rules/typescript.md` requires *"an inline comment explaining why the value is guaranteed non-null at that point"*, and there is none. Notable because this PR's commit message is specifically about *removing* a non-null assertion. `(basket.couponItems ?? []).map(...)` sidesteps it entirely.
Also at `:86`: an unused `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` directive (warn) — dead, the rule doesn't fire on `:87`.
Severity: **Should-fix**. Confidence: **high** — measured.

**9. `order-summary/index.tsx:229` — `key={adjustment.priceAdjustmentId}` on an optional field, with the fallback pattern applied 45 lines later but not here.**
Mechanism: `ShopperBasketsTypes.PriceAdjustment.priceAdjustmentId?: string` and `price?: number` — both optional (verified in `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`, ShopperBaskets namespace). React accepts `undefined` as a key, so two custom/manual adjustments without ids collide and reconcile wrongly. The override *does* add `?? index` for shipping adjustments at `:273-275` — so the author knew the pattern and applied it inconsistently. Inherited from base `:179`, but this is a new file, so it's fair game.
Severity: **Nit**. Confidence: **high**.

**10. i18n — untranslated, PDP-namespaced Was/Now strings now reach cart, checkout, confirmation and order history.**
Detail and search scope in §C. Two new `order_summary.*` ids are also at 0 coverage.
Severity: **Should-fix** (needs an Integration/SI conversation, not a code change — `translations/` is Tier 2). Confidence: **high**.

**11. Visual inconsistency within a single cart — discounted prices render 14px/500/green, undiscounted 16px/bold/black.**
Values and derivation in §C. Plus the sub-AA `#969696` PDP exception silently extended to four new surfaces.
Severity: **Should-fix**, but needs UI-designer input — do not let anyone guess a number here. Confidence: **high on the token values** (read from source); **medium on the 16px** (inferred from `theme/index.ts:60` replacing `styles.global` and `globalStyles.ts` setting no `body` `fontSize` — not measured in a browser).

**Smaller, all verified:**

## What I could not verify

1. **Whether any Zimmermann master has no `color` variation attribute, or all-unorderable colours** (finding 5's trigger) — needs a live SFCC/BM check.
2. **Whether any master has a third variation axis** (D4's `find`-picks-first edge) — same.

content.text:
## PR #118 — review findings

**State, re-read just now:** OPEN, head `1a32bc94`, mergeable but `BLOCKED`, `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`, 0 unresolved threads. CodeRabbit's last review was on `829bdc1a` then dismissed, but head is a pure rebase of it (all six code blobs byte-identical), so its review still applies to what's there now.

### Gates — head vs base, measured both sides

| Gate | Base `63855e6e` | Head `1a32bc94` | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean | none |
| `npm run test` | 105 files / 1536 tests pass | 107 files / 1551 tests pass | +2 files, +15 tests, all pass |
| `npm run lint` | 1297 problems | 1821 problems | **+524**, of which 516 are prettier formatting |
| `audit:tokens` | 6 unacknowledged | 11 unacknowledged | **+5**, all carried verbatim from the base SFCC files |

CI on head: Unit tests and Storybook **passed**. Playwright E2E and BrowserStack **skipped** — the change-scoped skip, so they prove nothing. Deploy Preview succeeded, which is what let me verify the rest live.

---

### The blocker: the checkout order summary is broken on this PR's own preview

**Consequence.** On the checkout page, the order summary's cart-items panel renders with **no product thumbnail and no colour/size line**. The item name only survives because the basket itself carries it.

**Mechanism.** Commit `18bcfa30` added a hand-written SCAPI field selector to narrow the product query. The `imageGroups[viewType=small]` bracket predicate is not valid selector grammar. Every one of those calls returns **HTTP 400**, `products` comes back undefined, and the panel renders from the basket line alone. The error is swallowed, so nothing tells the shopper or the developer.

**How I know.** Three ways. I replayed the exact shipped parameters against the live SCAPI proxy and got `400 Malformed Selector`, with the brackets both percent-encoded and raw, so it isn't an artefact of my test. I bisected it: removing only `[viewType=small]` returns `200`, every other clause is valid alone. Then I reproduced it end to end on the deployed preview at `/checkout` with a real item in the basket, and read the missing image and missing attributes straight out of the DOM. That's the screenshot above.

**Surface.** `showCartItems={true}` comes only from the base checkout and checkout-one-click pages, and neither is overridden, so this is the live checkout sidebar. The cart page renders the summary without cart items, so the cart page is fine.

**Fix.** Drop the bracket predicate. One character class.

The irony worth naming: this came from a CodeRabbit performance suggestion, and CodeRabbit then marked the thread resolved.

---

### Everything else, ranked by what it costs to ignore

**1. Two ACs are simply not built.** `item-price.tsx` — SFCC-645 AC3 and SFCC-778 AC4/AC5 all require a promotional label beneath the cart line ("X% off applied" / "Private Sale — 20% Off Applied"). Nothing in the diff renders one. `ZimmProductPrice` has exactly two strings, Was and Now. **CONFIRMED**, in-scope.

**2. The summary line is missing the percentage the AC asks for.** `order-summary/index.tsx:226` renders `{itemText} Applied` plus the amount. SFCC-645 AC5 asks for name **and percentage** and amount, with a worked example. The PR body says the flat format "matches the confirmed AC" and justifies it as simplifying the base's "discount-type branching logic (percentage vs fixed-amount)". The base is one line, `<Text>{adjustment.itemText}</Text>`, with no branching at all — I diffed it. So the stated reason for dropping the percentage isn't true, and no doc in `.docs/` confirms a flat format. **CONFIRMED**, in-scope.

**3. The colour-switch guard treats a live selection as stale.** `product-detail/index.tsx:497` — pick a size, switch colour, and the size dropdown **still shows the size you picked**, because `ProductView` never resets `localSizeValue`. But the pricing memo sees `selectedSizeSelection.colour !== urlColour`, throws the size away, and falls back to colour-range pricing, so Was/Now disappears while the UI says a full variant is selected. I proved the state desync in the browser on two products. **CodeRabbit raised exactly this and withdrew it** on the reasoning that ProductView retains the selection, "so the finding's claim was incorrect" — retention is the very thing that makes the guard wrong. The withdrawal inverted the problem instead of dissolving it. Mechanism **CONFIRMED**; the wrong-number-on-screen consequence is **PLAUSIBLE** only, because I couldn't find a product on that environment that is both multi-colour and has per-size sale pricing.

**4. Zero test coverage on the part that broke.** The new `order-summary/index.test.tsx` never sets `showCartItems`, so `CartItems` and the whole product-fetch path never render in any test. The author documented why honestly — Vitest can't load the base contexts chain, and `vitest.config.ts` is Tier 1. That's a real harness gap, not carelessness, but it is exactly why the 400 shipped. The 7 tests and 4 stories cover shipping-promo aggregation and shipping totals; **nothing** touches `orderPriceAdjustments`, which is the ticket's actual deliverable. **CONFIRMED**, in-scope.

**5. Discounted and undiscounted cart lines render at different type.** Measured on the live preview: undiscounted line is **16px / 700 / black**; the new branch is **14px / 500**, Was grey `#969696`, Now green `#2d5a3d`. Two adjacent rows in one cart would disagree on size, weight and colour. Needs the designer, not a guessed number. **CONFIRMED** on both numbers.

**6. A fabricated `A$0.00`.** `order-summary/index.tsx:218` and `:368` — `productSubTotal ?? 0` renders a confident zero for an unknown total, while the same file uses "TBD" for unknown shipping and tax, and the story file states the principle in so many words: "TBD, not a fabricated $0.00". **CONFIRMED**, in-scope.

**7. Storybook renders the wrong component.** `order-summary/index.tsx:29` imports item-price from the SFCC base path for a component this PR overrides. `.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`, so the four new stories exercise the **base** item-price with no Was/Now. `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents this exact trap. One-word fix to a relative path. **CONFIRMED**.

**8. The registry files go backwards.** `.claude/registry/*.md` were regenerated before the rebase. `Last updated` moves **backwards** against develop, and committed "Last touched" dates get reverted on files this PR never touched. Merging overwrites develop's newer generated data. `npm run generate:registry` fixes it. **CONFIRMED**.

**Recorded, not worth posting:** the +5 `audit:tokens` hits are all base SFCC values copied verbatim under the copy-first rule, so true as a fact and unfair as criticism; a stale comment naming `selectedSizeValue` instead of `selectedSizeSelection`; an uncommented `couponItems!`; a dead eslint-disable.

---

### Scope verdict

It **under-delivers** on both named tickets (no item label, no percentage, PLP untouched for SFCC-778 AC2) and **over-delivers** four things no AC asks for: the shipping-TBD state, multi-shipment promo aggregation, the coupon-remove guard, and the query narrowing. All four came from CodeRabbit comments on this PR. So the scope drift wasn't the author freelancing — it was him doing what the bot asked, and one of those four is the blocker.

Separately: the PDP fix is a defect repair on SFCC-194, which is already **In SIT**, landing inside a PR titled for 645/778.

---

### What nobody verified

## F1 — BLOCKING. The base-path import means `order-summary` renders the **base** `item-price` in *every* environment, including the shipped app — and that fails a named AC

`overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.tsx:29`
```ts
import CartItemVariantPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price'
```

**Rule:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` § "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component" — import B via a relative path, not the SFCC base path.

**The doc understates this, and I verified the resolver directly** rather than trusting either the doc or a source read. I instantiated the real `OverridesResolverPlugin` (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`) exactly as `configs/webpack/config.js:151-156` does, pointed it at the PR-head tree, and replayed the actual request:

| Issuer | Request | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/order-summary/` | base path → item-price | **BASE `node_modules` .jsx** |
| `node_modules/.../order-summary/` | base path → item-price | override `.tsx` |
| `node_modules/.../checkout/` | base path → order-summary | override `.tsx` |

The cause is `isFromExtends()`'s second condition, `!filepath.includes(issuerPath)` — the redirect is **deliberately skipped when the issuer is inside `overrides/`**, and the plugin's own comment says so: *"This will return false if the issuer is a file in the overrides dir… allows the overrides to import from the base template using the same syntax."*

So the answer to your question 1 is: **none of the three resolve to the override.** Not the real app build, not `.storybook/main.js` (which aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` → `node_modules`, no resolver), not `vitest.config.ts` (no alias for that package at all). `overrideStyling.md`'s claim that a base-path import "will build and run correctly in the shipped app" is **wrong** — worth a separate doc fix, since it would let the next person make this exact mistake believing only Storybook/Vitest were affected.

**What the PR's own test and story actually exercise: neither component's new code.** Both files leave `showCartItems` at its `false` default, so `CartItems` — the only thing that renders `CartItemVariantPrice` — never mounts. Proven with coverage rather than by reading: `vitest run overrides/app/components/order-summary --coverage.all=false` produces **no coverage entry for `item-variant/item-price.tsx` at all** (the module is never even loaded), and `order-summary/index.tsx` itself sits at **50.48% statements (155/307)**.

**Concrete consequence — a named AC fails.** SFCC-778's AC (`customfield_10231`) reads:
> *"…when they view **the order summary**, then Was/Now pricing is displayed per line item and the promotional label is shown."*

Because of this one import, the order-summary line items get the base component — flat price, `listPrice: null`, no Was/Now. `.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md` §3 (PRC-09) names the same surfaces: *"Original list price displayed alongside active sale price — shown on PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist…"*

**Fix:** `import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price'`. I verified a relative request is not intercepted by the plugin at all, so plain webpack resolution picks up the local `.tsx`.

**Confidence: very high** (resolver executed, not inferred; coverage-proven; AC quoted verbatim).

Same for `OrderSummaryProps` (`order-summary/index.tsx:161-167`) vs base `index.jsx:350-356`: all five props present, `fontSize` correctly narrowed to the same five literals. **No prop is rejected or dropped.** Credit where due.

**Behaviour is not faithful.** Exhaustive grep — **scope: every file under `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`, plus the whole package outside `app/`** (zero hits there) — found 8 importers of `item-price`, **all 8 using the SFCC base path, none relative**:

## F4 — MAJOR. The `ZimmProductPrice` branch drops the base component's screen-reader labelling, and makes every discounted cart line a live region

`item-price.tsx:99-107`.

Base `DisplayPrice` → `current-price.jsx:30-67` / `list-price.jsx:31-63` each render (a) an `aria-label` on the visible figure — *"current price $240.00"* / *"was price $300.00"* rather than a bare number — and (b) a `VisuallyHidden` node that prefixes `labelForA11y` (the product name) so, per their own comment, *"the product name is announced before the price to avoid confusion"*.

The new branch passes neither. `ZimmProductPrice` has no `labelForA11y` prop and its docblock says so explicitly — *"this atom has no such prefix to order"* — reasoning entirely about the PDP, where the product name is the `<h1>` and there is one price on the page. In a multi-line cart or order summary that premise doesn't hold: a screen-reader user hears *"Was $300.00 Now $240.00"* with nothing binding it to a product.

Second, `isLive={true}` (`item-price.tsx:106`) is passed explicitly even though it is already the default — so every discounted line becomes a polite live region. `ZimmProductPrice`'s own prop doc says the opposite for this shape: *"Pass `false` when this atom is reused inside a grid of many cards (e.g. a PLP) where the price never changes after mount, so a live region adds DOM/AT overhead for no benefit."* A cart line-item list is that shape.

**Rule:** AGENTS.md § Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA); `overrideStyling.md` § bridge pattern (faithful default export).
**Confidence: high** on the dropped labelling (read both base sub-components); **medium** on the live-region severity — I did not test with a real screen reader.

## F5 — MAJOR. Set/master cart lines silently lose the range ("From X") treatment when discounted

`item-price.tsx:99` — the branch condition is `variant?.itemId && isOnSale`, with no `isASet`/`isMaster` guard:

```ts
{variant?.itemId && isOnSale ? ( <ZimmProductPrice … /> ) : variant?.itemId ? ( <DisplayPrice … /> ) : …}
```

`isASet`/`isMaster` are computed (`:55-56`) and threaded into `priceData` (`:76-78`) — but for a discounted line the first branch always wins and `priceData` is never read. Base `display-price/index.jsx:67-72` branches on exactly those flags to render the range form. So a set or master line on promotion now renders a flat `Was/Now` instead of `From X`.

Every fixture in `item-price.test.tsx` uses `type: {}` (`:71`), so no test catches it.

**Related, and provably dead:** `listPrice: isOnSale ? price : null` (`item-price.tsx:66`) plus its two-line justification comment has **zero runtime effect**. That `priceData` only reaches `DisplayPrice` on the `itemId && !isOnSale` branch, where `isOnSale` is false by construction — so `listPrice` is always `null` there, identical to the base. The Was/Now comes entirely from `ZimmProductPrice`. The line reads as the mechanism for overriding the base's `listPrice: null`; it isn't.

Consequently the JSDoc at `:45-47` and the comment at `:64-65` are both inaccurate: they say the original price is *"shown **crossed out**"*, but `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:136-153` renders *"Was $X Now $Y"* as muted text labels, and `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:30` has `wasPrice: {}` — **no `textDecoration` anywhere in the recipe**. Nothing is crossed out on the path that executes.

**Confidence: very high** (branch reachability is mechanical; verified the recipe has no strikethrough).

## CLAIM 1 — `productSubTotal` excludes order-level adjustments

**Verdict: CONFIRMED.**

The consequence first: if you read `productSubTotal` as "what the customer's basket of goods costs after every discount," you will under-report the discount and over-report what's left to pay — for the claim's own numbers, you'd think the customer still owes 1000 when they actually owe 800. That's the exact bug shape this field name invites.

Mechanism, from source — `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts` (package version `5.2.0`, matching the pin in `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/package.json:44`, so this is genuinely what this project resolves, not a stale copy):

- `Basket.productSubTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7040`: *"The total price of all products including item-level adjustments, **but not including order-level adjustments** or shipping charges."*
- `Basket.productTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7042`: *"The total price of all products including adjustments, but not including shipping charges."* — the sibling `Shipment` type's equivalent field (`index.esm.d.ts:6667`) spells the same fact out unambiguously: *"including item-level adjustments **and prorated order-level adjustments**."*
- `Basket.orderTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7034`: *"The total price, including products, shipping and tax."*
- `Basket.orderPriceAdjustments`, `index.esm.d.ts:7032`: *"The order-level price adjustments"* — a sibling field, not something `productSubTotal` folds in.

I checked this held for `Order` (post-checkout) too, since `order-summary/index.tsx`'s own comment says it renders both baskets and orders: `Order.productSubTotal`/`productTotal`/`orderTotal` at `index.esm.d.ts:33414-33477` carry the identical semantics (one field's doc comment has a stray "in the shipment" copy-paste artifact from the `Shipment` type, but the "not including order-level adjustments" clause is intact and unchanged).

So, applying this to the claim's own numbers — one line at `price: 1000`, order-level promo `-200`:
- `productSubTotal` = **1000** (item-level only; order-level excluded — matches the claim exactly)
- `productTotal` = **800** (1000, then the −200 order-level adjustment prorated in)
- `orderTotal` = `productTotal` + `shippingTotal` + `taxTotal` = 800 + shipping + tax (not fully computable without those two numbers, but the relationship is unambiguous)

**What I could not settle:** I found no committed fixture/mock JSON anywhere in the repo (searched all `.json`/`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js` outside `node_modules` for `productSubTotal`/`orderPriceAdjustments`) showing a real captured basket response with these three numbers side by side — the only matches were the SDK's own type declarations and `order-summary/index.tsx` itself. So this is settled from the SDK's embedded API contract, not a live-captured example. A live sandbox basket with a real order-level promotion applied would be the only strictly stronger source than this — but the type doc is the API provider's own contract, not a guess, so I don't think that gap weakens the verdict.

`.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md:63` reads verbatim: *"Customer-group-specific catalogue pricing — visible on PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended tiles, wishlist (**not cart-only discounts**). Discounts do not apply to products already on sale or to gift cards."* That's an exact match for the claim's seven surfaces and the "cart-only discounts" distinction — **CONFIRMED** as text.

The sentence at line 63 carries **no inline ID** — unusual, since almost every other bullet in this same document tags itself (`PRC-09`, `PRC-18`, etc.). The section header at line 61 claims a range, `## 5. VIC & Customer Group Pricing (PRC-17 – PRC-19)`. Of that range, `PRC-18` and `PRC-19` are both explicitly spoken for by two *later, different* sentences (lines 73–74: the no-stacking-on-sale rule, and the BM priority-rules config). That leaves `PRC-17` as the only number in the header's range not yet claimed by anything in section 5 — except the document's own Section 7 Open Items (line 96) explicitly assigns `PRC-17` to something else entirely: *"Platinum VIC permanent discount rate — TBC (PRC-17)"* — a fact about one table row, not the visibility statement. ```

**Rule:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` § "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component" — import B via a relative path, not the SFCC base path.

**The doc understates this, and I verified the resolver directly** rather than trusting either the doc or a source read. I instantiated the real `OverridesResolverPlugin` (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`) exactly as `configs/webpack/config.js:151-156` does, pointed it at the PR-head tree, and replayed the actual request:

| Issuer | Request | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|

| `node_modules/.../order-summary/` | base path → item-price | override `.tsx` |

The cause is `isFromExtends()`'s second condition, `!filepath.includes(issuerPath)` — the redirect is **deliberately skipped when the issuer is inside `overrides/`**, and the plugin's own comment says so: *"This will return false if the issuer is a file in the overrides dir… allows the overrides to import from the base template using the same syntax."*

| `node_modules/.../order-summary/` | base path → item-price | override `.tsx` |
| `node_modules/.../checkout/` | base path → order-summary | override `.tsx` |

The cause is `isFromExtends()`'s second condition, `!filepath.includes(issuerPath)` — the redirect is **deliberately skipped when the issuer is inside `overrides/`**, and the plugin's own comment says so: *"This will return false if the issuer is a file in the overrides dir… allows the overrides to import from the base template using the same syntax."*

## CLAIM 1 — `productSubTotal` excludes order-level adjustments

**Verdict: CONFIRMED.**

The consequence first: if you read `productSubTotal` as "what the customer's basket of goods costs after every discount," you will under-report the discount and over-report what's left to pay — for the claim's own numbers, you'd think the customer still owes 1000 when they actually owe 800. That's the exact bug shape this field name invites.

Mechanism, from source — `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts` (package version `5.2.0`, matching the pin in `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/package.json:44`, so this is genuinely what this project resolves, not a stale copy):

- `Basket.productSubTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7040`: *"The total price of all products including item-level adjustments, **but not including order-level adjustments** or shipping charges."*
- `Basket.productTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7042`: *"The total price of all products including adjustments, but not including shipping charges."* — the sibling `Shipment` type's equivalent field (`index.esm.d.ts:6667`) spells the same fact out unambiguously: *"including item-level adjustments **and prorated order-level adjustments**."*
- `Basket.orderTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7034`: *"The total price, including products, shipping and tax."*
- `Basket.orderPriceAdjustments`, `index.esm.d.ts:7032`: *"The order-level price adjustments"* — a sibling field, not something `productSubTotal` folds in.

I checked this held for `Order` (post-checkout) too, since `order-summary/index.tsx`'s own comment says it renders both baskets and orders: `Order.productSubTotal`/`productTotal`/`orderTotal` at `index.esm.d.ts:33414-33477` carry the identical semantics (one field's doc comment has a stray "in the shipment" copy-paste artifact from the `Shipment` type, but the "not including order-level adjustments" clause is intact and unchanged).

So, applying this to the claim's own numbers — one line at `price: 1000`, order-level promo `-200`:
- `productSubTotal` = **1000** (item-level only; order-level excluded — matches the claim exactly)
- `productTotal` = **800** (1000, then the −200 order-level adjustment prorated in)
- `orderTotal` = `productTotal` + `shippingTotal` + `taxTotal` = 800 + shipping + tax (not fully computable without those two numbers, but the relationship is unambiguous)

**What I could not settle:** I found no committed fixture/mock JSON anywhere in the repo (searched all `.json`/`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js` outside `node_modules` for `productSubTotal`/`orderPriceAdjustments`) showing a real captured basket response with these three numbers side by side — the only matches were the SDK's own type declarations and `order-summary/index.tsx` itself. So this is settled from the SDK's embedded API contract, not a live-captured example. A live sandbox basket with a real order-level promotion applied would be the only strictly stronger source than this — but the type doc is the API provider's own contract, not a guess, so I don't think that gap weakens the verdict.

## F1 — BLOCKING. The base-path import means `order-summary` renders the **base** `item-price` in *every* environment, including the shipped app — and that fails a named AC

`overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.tsx:29`
```ts
import CartItemVariantPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price'
```

**Rule:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` § "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component" — import B via a relative path, not the SFCC base path.

**The doc understates this, and I verified the resolver directly** rather than trusting either the doc or a source read. I instantiated the real `OverridesResolverPlugin` (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`) exactly as `configs/webpack/config.js:151-156` does, pointed it at the PR-head tree, and replayed the actual request:

| Issuer | Request | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/order-summary/` | base path → item-price | **BASE `node_modules` .jsx** |
| `node_modules/.../order-summary/` | base path → item-price | override `.tsx` |
| `node_modules/.../checkout/` | base path → order-summary | override `.tsx` |

The cause is `isFromExtends()`'s second condition, `!filepath.includes(issuerPath)` — the redirect is **deliberately skipped when the issuer is inside `overrides/`**, and the plugin's own comment says so: *"This will return false if the issuer is a file in the overrides dir… allows the overrides to import from the base template using the same syntax."*

So the answer to your question 1 is: **none of the three resolve to the override.** Not the real app build, not `.storybook/main.js` (which aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` → `node_modules`, no resolver), not `vitest.config.ts` (no alias for that package at all). `overrideStyling.md`'s claim that a base-path import "will build and run correctly in the shipped app" is **wrong** — worth a separate doc fix, since it would let the next person make this exact mistake believing only Storybook/Vitest were affected.

**What the PR's own test and story actually exercise: neither component's new code.** Both files leave `showCartItems` at its `false` default, so `CartItems` — the only thing that renders `CartItemVariantPrice` — never mounts. Proven with coverage rather than by reading: `vitest run overrides/app/components/order-summary --coverage.all=false` produces **no coverage entry for `item-variant/item-price.tsx` at all** (the module is never even loaded), and `order-summary/index.tsx` itself sits at **50.48% statements (155/307)**.

**Concrete consequence — a named AC fails.** SFCC-778's AC (`customfield_10231`) reads:
> *"…when they view **the order summary**, then Was/Now pricing is displayed per line item and the promotional label is shown."*

Because of this one import, the order-summary line items get the base component — flat price, `listPrice: null`, no Was/Now. `.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md` §3 (PRC-09) names the same surfaces: *"Original list price displayed alongside active sale price — shown on PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist…"*

**Fix:** `import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price'`. I verified a relative request is not intercepted by the plugin at all, so plain webpack resolution picks up the local `.tsx`.

**Confidence: very high** (resolver executed, not inferred; coverage-proven; AC quoted verbatim).

`item-price.tsx:99-107`.

Base `DisplayPrice` → `current-price.jsx:30-67` / `list-price.jsx:31-63` each render (a) an `aria-label` on the visible figure — *"current price $240.00"* / *"was price $300.00"* rather than a bare number — and (b) a `VisuallyHidden` node that prefixes `labelForA11y` (the product name) so, per their own comment, *"the product name is announced before the price to avoid confusion"*.

That's the exact bug shape this field name invites.

Mechanism, from source — `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts` (package version `5.2.0`, matching the pin in `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/package.json:44`, so this is genuinely what this project resolves, not a stale copy):

- `Basket.productSubTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7040`: *"The total price of all products including item-level adjustments, **but not including order-level adjustments** or shipping charges."*
- `Basket.productTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7042`: *"The total price of all products including adjustments, but not including shipping charges."* — the sibling `Shipment` type's equivalent field (`index.esm.d.ts:6667`) spells the same fact out unambiguously: *"including item-level adjustments **and prorated order-level adjustments**."*
- `Basket.orderTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7034`: *"The total price, including products, shipping and tax."*
- `Basket.orderPriceAdjustments`, `index.esm.d.ts:7032`: *"The order-level price adjustments"* — a sibling field, not something `productSubTotal` folds in.

- `productTotal` = **800** (1000, then the −200 order-level adjustment prorated in)
- `orderTotal` = `productTotal` + `shippingTotal` + `taxTotal` = 800 + shipping + tax (not fully computable without those two numbers, but the relationship is unambiguous)

content.text:
## First, a correction to what I told you

I said finding 7 was "Storybook renders the wrong component." **That was too soft.** It's a second blocker.

**Consequence.** On the live checkout page, the order summary's line items will **never** show Was/Now. Not in Storybook, not in tests, not in production. Ever. That's SFCC-778's AC5 and SFCC-645's AC7 failing by construction, on the exact surface those ACs name.

**Mechanism.** One line: `order-summary/index.tsx:29` imports item-price by its Salesforce package path instead of a relative path. The webpack plugin that swaps base components for our overrides has a deliberate rule — if the file *making* the import lives inside `overrides/`, it does **not** swap. The plugin says so in its own comment: *"This will return false if the issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* It exists so an override can still reach the real base file when it wants to. Here we didn't want to.

So: the cart page gets the new price component, because the file importing it there lives in `node_modules`. The checkout summary doesn't, because the file importing it there is ours.

**Fix.** Change `'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price'` to `'../item-variant/item-price'`. One word.

**And our own rule doc is wrong about this.** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` says a base-path import *"will build and run correctly in the shipped app, but silently render the unstyled base version in Storybook and Vitest."* Only the second half is true. That's a separate fix, and it matters — that sentence would let the next person make this same mistake on purpose.

---

Now, your two questions.

## Question 1 — the verdict

**What's actually on the table.** There are two things wrong that a shopper would see, and both have one-line fixes:

1. The checkout summary shows no product photo and no colour/size, because a hand-written API field filter has a syntax error and returns 400.
2. The checkout summary will never show Was/Now, because of the import above.

Both are on the checkout page. Both are in the same file. Both were written in the last two commits.

**Why the choice matters.** "Request changes" on GitHub is a formal state. It blocks merge until *you* clear it, and it's visible to the whole team. "Comment" leaves the gate entirely to the code-owner review that's already required — Squad A and Squad B are both requested, and the Tier 2 approval that `order-summary/` needs was dismissed by the last push, so it has to be re-obtained anyway.

**The real trade-off** is not whether the bugs get fixed — they will either way, because two named reviewers still have to approve. It's about **who is on the hook for catching them**. If you comment only, and a code owner approves without reading your comments closely, the 400 ships to SIT. If you request changes, it can't.

The counter-argument is register: Jersey is lateral, not junior. Both of these came from him doing exactly what CodeRabbit told him to do — the API filter was a CodeRabbit performance suggestion, and CodeRabbit then marked the thread resolved. He wasn't freelancing.

My read: **the formal block is right, and it isn't a judgement on him.** A reproducible checkout regression is the textbook case for it, and you can say plainly in the comment that both findings trace to bot suggestions rather than his own scoping.

## Question 2 — where the AC gap goes

**What the gap is.** Three ACs ask for things that don't exist in the code:

- An "X% off applied" label under each cart item. Nothing renders it.
- The discount **percentage** in the summary line. It renders name and amount only.
- Was/Now on the PLP product card for SFCC-778. Not touched.

**Why it isn't simply "Jersey missed it."** Three reasons, and they compound.

First, the PR body says the flat no-percentage format "matches the confirmed AC." I looked — no document in `.docs/` says that. The one format spec that does exist, `checkout.md:211`, **includes** a percentage: `"DISCOUNT | GOLD VIP - 10% OFF"`. So either he's working from a verbal confirmation nobody wrote down, or he read the AC differently.

Second, Hazel opened two questions on SFCC-778 in the last 24 hours that nobody has answered. One asks whether AC4 conflicts with an AC on SFCC-38. The other says FED needs to check that promotions only apply on the storefronts configured in BM — which is work this PR doesn't do and wasn't asked to do when it was written.

Third, and this is the one that could invalidate the whole approach: `pricing-currency-globale.md:63` says customer-group pricing is **catalogue** pricing, visible everywhere, and explicitly *"not cart-only discounts."* This PR implements it as a cart-only order-level adjustment. If that line is right, the mechanism is wrong, not just the label.

**So the question is really: do you ask the author to defend an AC he didn't write, or do you settle the requirement first?** Asking him puts him in the position of arguing with a ticket. Settling it with Hazel first means he waits, but waits on the right answer.

There's also a third thing worth knowing: SFCC-778 is **assigned to Gideon**, not Jersey. Jersey is the assignee on 645 only. So on 778 he's delivering someone else's ticket.
